overall: The letter ڠ (nga) appears several times, and ف may stand for ڤ. That points to a Southeast Asian Jawi-type spelling rather than Arabic, Persian or Kurdish. A few Arabic religious words (huwa, Muhammad, baraka, kufr) sit inside short groups that look like Malay or Tausug pronouns (kamu, -mu, kaw). The text could be an amulet or charm formula, or a short devotional or personal inscription. I could not get a running reading, and many of the groups are probably noise or broken words.
language_guess: A Malay-world language in Jawi script (Malay, or a Philippine Jawi such as Tausug or Maranao), with Arabic religious words mixed in
